name: dynare
desc: Platform for economic models, particularly DSGE and OLG models
why: Solves dynamic macroeconomic models like DSGE, a real simulation platform, though the field is specialised and the pull is moderate.

brief.what_it_is: Dynare is a platform for building and running economic models, mainly DSGE (dynamic stochastic general equilibrium) and OLG (overlapping generations) models. The author says you write the model almost as you would on paper, and Dynare handles the solving. The homepage lists solving and estimating a model, computing optimal policy, identification and sensitivity analysis, and perfect-foresight simulation as tasks. It runs on top of MATLAB, GNU Octave, or Julia. The homepage does not say what the inputs or outputs look like in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to make macroeconomic modelling easy to use: write the model in near-paper form and let the tool do the solving and estimation work.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the mechanism. The package metadata lists a dynare-preprocessor executable, which suggests a preprocessing step that translates the model file before it runs in the host language, but I could not confirm this from the pages I read.
brief.install_notes: The Homebrew caveat says that to get started, you open Octave and type: addpath $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/dynare/lib/dynare/matlab. So the Homebrew install needs GNU Octave (or MATLAB) plus that addpath step before Dynare is usable. The homepage's 'Platforms' section names MATLAB, GNU Octave, and Julia as hosts. I did not see documentation on other setup steps.
brief.standout: Its pitch is a model language that reads close to the equations on paper, with one tool covering solving, estimation, policy and sensitivity work. It is also free, open-source software for a field where many tools are commercial or closed.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the homepage. It lists a Dynare 7.2 release dated 11 September 2026, a 7.1 release dated 28 May 2026, and a 2026 advanced users workshop. It is hosted by CEPREMAP and sponsored by DSGE-net and fiscal sponsorship under NumFOCUS. I could not check a GitHub commit history.
brief.caveats: Most, not all, source files are GPL v3 or later, per the homepage. The main host platform, MATLAB, is commercial, so the free route depends on Octave or Julia. I could not load the GitHub README. Three guessed GitHub URLs returned 404, so no README command lines were checked. The commands_seen list is empty for that reason, not because none exist. The homepage's 'Documentation' link was not followed because I did not have its URL. The scout note calls the field specialised, which matches the homepage's focus on macroeconomists.
quotes: Write your model almost as you would on paper and Dynare will take care of the rest!
Dynare is free and open-source software and most of the source files are covered by the GNU General Public Licence version 3 or later.
Dynare runs on top of MATLAB, GNU Octave, and Julia!
